entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 38 Jr 38:1-28 . Jeremiah Predicts the Capture of Jerusalem, for Which He Is Cast into a Dungeon, but Is Transferred to the Prison Court on the Intercession of Ebed-melech, and Has a Secret Interview with Zedekiah. All this was subsequent to his imprisonment in Jonathan's house, and his release on his interview with Zedekiah. The latter occurred before the return of the Chaldeans to the siege; the similar events in this chapter occurred after it. 1. Jucal-- Jehucal ( Jr 37:3 ). Pashur-- ( Jr 21:1 ; compare Jr 21:9 with Jr 38:2 ). The deputation in Jr 21:1 , to whom Jeremiah gave this reply, if not identical with the hearers of Jeremiah ( Jr 38:1 ), must have been sent just before the latter "heard" him speaking the same words. Zephaniah is not mentioned here as in Jr 21:1 , but is so in Jr 37:3 . Jucal is mentioned here and in the previous deputation ( Jr 37:3 ), but not in Jr 21:1 . Shephatiah and Gedaliah here do not occur either in Jr 21:1 or Jr 37:3 . The identity of his words in both cases is natural, when uttered, at a very short interval, and one of the hearers (Pashur) being present on both occasions. unto all the people-- They had free access to him in the court of the prison ( Jr 32:12 ).

It was not a subterranean prison as that in Jonathan's house (<reference osisRef="Jer.37.15">Jr 37:15</reference>), but a pit or cistern, which had been full of water, but was emptied of it during the siege, so that only "mire" remained. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10433"/><div sID="gen18606" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10433"/><hi type="bold">7. Ebed-melech--</hi>The Hebrew designation given this Ethiopian, meaning "king's servant." Already, even at this early time, God wished to show what good reason there was for calling the Gentiles to salvation. An Ethiopian stranger saves the prophet whom his own countrymen, the Jews, tried to destroy. So the Gentiles believed in Christ whom the Jews crucified, and Ethiopians were among the earliest converts (<reference osisRef="Acts.2.10">Ac 2:10</reference>, 41; 8:27-39). Ebed-melech probably was keeper of the royal harem, and so had private access to the king. The eunuchs over harems in the present day are mostly from Nubia or Abyssinia. <div eID="gen18606" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10435"/><div sID="gen18608" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10435"/><hi type="bold">9. die for hunger in the place where he is; for ... no ... bread in ... city--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Jer.37.21">Jr 37:21</reference>). He had heretofore got a piece of bread supplied to him. "Seeing that there is the utmost want of bread in the city, so that even if he were at large, there could no more be regularly supplied to him, much less now in a place where none remember or pity him, so that he is likely to die for hunger." "No more bread," that is, no more left of the public store in the city (<reference osisRef="Jer.37.21">Jr 37:21</reference>); or, all but no bread left anywhere [Maurer]. <div eID="gen18608" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10439"/><div sID="gen18615" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10439"/><hi type="bold">14. third entry--</hi>The Hebrews in determining the position of places faced the east, which they termed "that which is in front"; the south was thus called "that which is on the right hand"; the north, "that which is on the left hand"; the west, "that which is behind." So beginning with the east they might term it the first or principal entry; the south the second entry; the north the "third entry" of the outer or inner court [Maurer]. The third gate of the temple facing the palace; for through it the entrance lay from the palace into the temple (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.10.5">1Ki 10:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.10.12">12</reference>). It was westward (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.16">1Ch 26:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.18">18</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.9.11">2Ch 9:11</reference>) [Grotius]. But in the future temple it is eastward (<reference osisRef="Ezek.46.1">Eze 46:1</reference>, 2, 8). <div eID="gen18615" type="x-p"/>

But in the future temple it is eastward ( Eze 46:1 , 2, 8).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10448"/><div sID="gen18628" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10448"/><hi type="bold">26. presented--</hi>literally, "made my supplication to fall"; implying supplication with humble prostration (see on <reference osisRef="Jer.36.7">Jr 36:7</reference>).<div eID="gen18628" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18629" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Jonathan's house--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Jer.37.15">Jr 37:15</reference>), different from Malchiah's dungeon (<reference osisRef="Jer.38.6">Jr 38:6</reference>). This statement was true, though not the whole truth; the princes had no right to the information; no sanction is given by Scripture here to Jeremiah's representation of this being the cause of his having come to the king. Fear drove him to it. Compare <reference osisRef="Gen.20.2">Ge 20:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.20.12">12</reference>; on the other hand, <reference osisRef="1Sam.16.2">1Sa 16:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Sam.16.5">5</reference>.<div eID="gen18629" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18630" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">left off speaking with--</hi>Hebrew, "were silent from him," that is, withdrawing from him they left him quiet (<reference osisRef="1Sam.7.8">1Sa 7:8</reference>, Margin). <div eID="gen18630" type="x-p"/>
